explanation:
[EFFECT]
Temperature has a strong, non-monotonic (inverted-U) effect on predicted hourly bike demand. As temperatures rise from very cold (around 1°C) through to warm conditions, demand climbs sharply — cold temperatures carry large negative contributions that can cut predicted rentals by more than half. The effect peaks at around 30–31°C (normalised value ~0.74–0.76), where temperature provides its greatest boost to demand. Beyond that point, at extreme heat (near 40°C), the contribution turns slightly negative again, meaning very high temperatures begin to mildly suppress demand.

[IMPORTANCE]
Temperature is the **2nd most important** feature in the model out of 9, with an importance score of 0.253 — well ahead of month, humidity, weather situation, and all others. Only the hour of the day (importance 0.889) has a stronger influence on predicted demand, making temperature the dominant weather-related driver.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Ensure higher bike availability and staffing during mild-to-warm periods (roughly 17–31°C), and scale back resources in cold winter conditions, as extreme cold is the single largest temperature-related drag on demand — even more so than rainy or very hot weather.
